answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a basalt as the anchor of the cost. A reef stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a thread hold...
